subject.title: feat(browser): add secure per-tab copilot panel

question: Should this bundled browser copilot be accepted as a permanent core/extension security boundary after the broad-subscription path is denied and the new pairing/tool-binding contracts receive owner approval?
rationale: The patch introduces a new privileged browser identity, persistent pairing metadata, and a plugin-context binding contract; the remaining defect is mechanically repairable, but accepting the permanent boundary and public contract requires owner intent.

options.title: Sponsor the hardened design
options.body: Require the narrow broad-subscription denial, regression coverage, and fresh post-rebase proof, then review the browser copilot as the supported bundled feature.

options.title: Keep the panel out of the bundled surface
options.body: Pause the feature and retain only any independently useful generic Gateway hardening if maintainers do not want this permanent browser-copilot contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the hardened design
recommendation.body: Require the narrow broad-subscription denial, regression coverage, and fresh post-rebase proof, then review the browser copilot as the supported bundled feature.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the current branch, are assigned on the item, and are the strongest available routing candidate for the security-sensitive feature boundary.
